# Rules retrieved
[P-HOURS] §2.1 Working hours
Teaching takes place Monday to Friday between 9:00 and 17:00, in eight one-hour slots. No classes are held on Saturdays or Sundays. A class outside these hours, or on a weekend, requires the prior written approval of the Head of Department.

[P-SWAP] §3.3 Swapping slots
Two faculty members may swap teaching slots with the consent of both. The timetable coordinator must be informed before the swap takes effect, and the swap must not break any other regulation.

[P-ONLINE] §3.4 Online and covered classes
A class may be held online, or taken by a colleague, only as a make-up arrangement and only with the approval of the Head of Department. No course may have more than two online classes in a semester.

[P-CREDITS] §2.4 Contact hours and credits
Contact hours follow the L-T-P structure of each course. A 4-credit theory course has four contact hours per week (three lectures and one tutorial); a 4-credit course with a laboratory has three lectures and one two-hour practical. All contact hours must appear in the weekly timetable.

[P-MAKEUP] §3.2 Make-up classes
A class missed because of the faculty member's absence (conference, leave, official duty or a personal appointment) must be rescheduled as a make-up class within two weeks of the missed class. Recurring unavailability declared for the whole semester creates no make-up obligation, because the timetable is built around it.

[P-AUTHORITY] §1.2 Who may request changes
A faculty member may request changes only to their own classes. The Head of Department may request changes for any class of the department. The lab in-charge reports the availability of laboratories. The timetable coordinator publishes the timetable. Students may report clashes through their class representative but may not request that a class be moved or cancelled.

[P-SWAP] §3.3 Swapping slots
Two faculty members may swap teaching slots with the consent of both. The timetable coordinator must be informed before the swap takes effect, and the swap must not break any other regulation.

[P-ONLINE] §3.4 Online and covered classes
A class may be held online, or taken by a colleague, only as a make-up arrangement and only with the approval of the Head of Department. No course may have more than two online classes in a semester.

[P-PREFS] §3.1 Teaching preferences
Faculty may state preferences about days and times, such as keeping mornings or a particular day free. Preferences are accommodated where the timetable allows, but they are not guaranteed and give way to commitments and to other faculty members' unavailability.

[P-MAKEUP] §3.2 Make-up classes
A class missed because of the faculty member's absence (conference, leave, official duty or a personal appointment) must be rescheduled as a make-up class within two weeks of the missed class. Recurring unavailability declared for the whole semester creates no make-up obligation, because the timetable is built around it.

[P-MAKEUP] §3.2 Make-up classes
A class missed because of the faculty member's absence (conference, leave, official duty or a personal appointment) must be rescheduled as a make-up class within two weeks of the missed class. Recurring unavailability declared for the whole semester creates no make-up obligation, because the timetable is built around it.

[P-CLASH] §5.1 Clash reports
Students who find that two of their registered courses clash report it through their class representative. The timetable office investigates every report within five working days and informs the students of the outcome.

[P-LOAD] §2.5 Teaching load
A full-time faculty member teaches at most sixteen contact hours per week. Guest faculty teach at most eight contact hours per week.

[P-ONLINE] §3.4 Online and covered classes
A class may be held online, or taken by a colleague, only as a make-up arrangement and only with the approval of the Head of Department. No course may have more than two online classes in a semester.

[P-CREDITS] §2.4 Contact hours and credits
Contact hours follow the L-T-P structure of each course. A 4-credit theory course has four contact hours per week (three lectures and one tutorial); a 4-credit course with a laboratory has three lectures and one two-hour practical. All contact hours must appear in the weekly timetable.

Students who find that two of their registered courses clash report it through their class representative. The timetable office investigates every report within five working days and informs the students of the outcome.

# Rules retrieved
[P-MAXCONSEC] §2.3 Consecutive teaching hours
No faculty member and no section may be scheduled for more than three consecutive teaching hours. After three hours in a row (back-to-back classes) there must be a break of at least one hour. A practical session counts one hour for each slot it occupies.

[P-CREDITS] §2.4 Contact hours and credits
Contact hours follow the L-T-P structure of each course. A 4-credit theory course has four contact hours per week (three lectures and one tutorial); a 4-credit course with a laboratory has three lectures and one two-hour practical. All contact hours must appear in the weekly timetable.

[P-ONLINE] §3.4 Online and covered classes
A class may be held online, or taken by a colleague, only as a make-up arrangement and only with the approval of the Head of Department. No course may have more than two online classes in a semester.

[P-LOAD] §2.5 Teaching load
A full-time faculty member teaches at most sixteen contact hours per week. Guest faculty teach at most eight contact hours per week.

[P-HOURS] §2.1 Working hours
Teaching takes place Monday to Friday between 9:00 and 17:00, in eight one-hour slots. No classes are held on Saturdays or Sundays. A class outside these hours, or on a weekend, requires the prior written approval of the Head of Department.

Checking a request:
- forbidden: doing what the request asks would break a rule shown (for

  row than the rules allow). Cite the rule and suggest a compliant
  alternative that still gives the sender most of what they want.
- needs_approval: allowed only with someone's approval under a rule shown

- allowed: no rule shown is broken. Preferences and unavailability are
  normally allowed. Put in obligations any rule that attaches a duty to the
  request (for example, a make-up class for a class missed because of an
  absence in specific weeks). Leave cited_rules empty unless a rule matters.

# Rules retrieved
[P-LABS] §4.1 Laboratories and equipment
Practical sessions are held in laboratories with the equipment the course requires. The lab in-charge reports laboratory closures for maintenance, and the sessions affected are moved to another suitable laboratory or slot.

[P-CREDITS] §2.4 Contact hours and credits
Contact hours follow the L-T-P structure of each course. A 4-credit theory course has four contact hours per week (three lectures and one tutorial); a 4-credit course with a laboratory has three lectures and one two-hour practical. All contact hours must appear in the weekly timetable.

[P-LOAD] §2.5 Teaching load
A full-time faculty member teaches at most sixteen contact hours per week. Guest faculty teach at most eight contact hours per week.

[P-MAKEUP] §3.2 Make-up classes
A class missed because of the faculty member's absence (conference, leave, official duty or a personal appointment) must be rescheduled as a make-up class within two weeks of the missed class. Recurring unavailability declared for the whole semester creates no make-up obligation, because the timetable is built around it.

[P-LUNCH] §2.2 Common lunch break
The hour from 13:00 to 14:00 is a common lunch break for all students and staff. No lecture, tutorial or practical may be scheduled in this hour. The lunch break cannot be waived by the department; only the Dean may grant an exception.

A faculty member may request changes only to their own classes. The Head of Department may request changes for any class of the department. The lab in-charge reports the availability of laboratories. The hour from 13:00 to 14:00 is a common lunch break for all students and staff. No lecture, tutorial or practical may be scheduled in this hour. The lunch break cannot be waived by the department; only the Dean may grant an exception.

[P-CREDITS] §2.4 Contact hours and credits
Contact hours follow the L-T-P structure of each course. A 4-credit theory course has four contact hours per week (three lectures and one tutorial); a 4-credit course with a laboratory has three lectures and one two-hour practical. All contact hours must appear in the weekly timetable.

[P-MAXCONSEC] §2.3 Consecutive teaching hours
No faculty member and no section may be scheduled for more than three consecutive teaching hours. After three hours in a row (back-to-back classes) there must be a break of at least one hour. A practical session counts one hour for each slot it occupies.

Reasons given for unavailability, such as medical or family matters, are confidential. The timetable office records only that a reason was given and, where required, verified; the reason itself is never published or shared.

[P-MAKEUP] §3.2 Make-up classes
A class missed because of the faculty member's absence (conference, leave, official duty or a personal appointment) must be rescheduled as a make-up class within two weeks of the missed class. Reasons given for unavailability, such as medical or family matters, are confidential. The timetable office records only that a reason was given and, where required, verified; the reason itself is never published or shared.

[P-ONLINE] §3.4 Online and covered classes
A class may be held online, or taken by a colleague, only as a make-up arrangement and only with the approval of the Head of Department. No course may have more than two online classes in a semester.

Contact hours follow the L-T-P structure of each course. A 4-credit theory course has four contact hours per week (three lectures and one tutorial); a 4-credit course with a laboratory has three lectures and one two-hour practical. All contact hours must appear in the weekly timetable.

[P-LOAD] §2.5 Teaching load
A full-time faculty member teaches at most sixteen contact hours per week. Guest faculty teach at most eight contact hours per week.

# Rules retrieved
[P-AUTHORITY] §1.2 Who may request changes
A faculty member may request changes only to their own classes. The Head of Department may request changes for any class of the department. The lab in-charge reports the availability of laboratories. The timetable coordinator publishes the timetable. Students may report clashes through their class representative but may not request that a class be moved or cancelled.

[P-HOURS] §2.1 Working hours
Teaching takes place Monday to Friday between 9:00 and 17:00, in eight one-hour slots. No classes are held on Saturdays or Sundays. A class outside these hours, or on a weekend, requires the prior written approval of the Head of Department.

[P-PREFS] §3.1 Teaching preferences
Faculty may state preferences about days and times, such as keeping mornings or a particular day free. Preferences are accommodated where the timetable allows, but they are not guaranteed and give way to commitments and to other faculty members' unavailability.

[P-SWAP] §3.3 Swapping slots

Checking a request:

  alternative that still gives the sender most of what they want.
- needs_approval: allowed only with someone's approval under a rule shown

- allowed: no rule shown is broken. Preferences and unavailability are

# Rules retrieved
[P-MAKEUP] §3.2 Make-up classes
A class missed because of the faculty member's absence (conference, leave, official duty or a personal appointment) must be rescheduled as a make-up class within two weeks of the missed class. Recurring unavailability declared for the whole semester creates no make-up obligation, because the timetable is built around it.

[P-ONLINE] §3.4 Online and covered classes
A class may be held online, or taken by a colleague, only as a make-up arrangement and only with the approval of the Head of Department. No course may have more than two online classes in a semester.

[P-HOURS] §2.1 Working hours
Teaching takes place Monday to Friday between 9:00 and 17:00, in eight one-hour slots. No classes are held on Saturdays or Sundays. A class outside these hours, or on a weekend, requires the prior written approval of the Head of Department.

[P-AUTHORITY] §1.2 Who may request changes
A faculty member may request changes only to their own classes. The Head of Department may request changes for any class of the department. The lab in-charge reports the availability of laboratories. The timetable coordinator publishes the timetable. Students may report clashes through their class representative but may not request that a class be moved or cancelled.

[P-LOAD] §2.5 Teaching load
